resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. research_claims §11 line 136: scope: The finding rests on a misreading of §11, gets its own count wrong, and proposes a fix that the format spec treats as a defect on due:none stamps.

(a) What the rule says. I read §11 at its current wording with `rule.js research_claims 11`. It requires the verification SECTION to list "(3) named fallback framing if specific source doesn't hold". It does not say every source needs its own fallback. The per-stamp `fallback:` slot comes from §11a's grammar and from `source-freshness-format.md`, and the judge did not cite §11a. The section does name a fallback for the exact failure the judge describes. L143 says every X quote "above" was verified through oEmbed, then gives "fallback: quote from the transcript and the mirrors instead of the X permalinks." That plan is written for the case where the tweets at L136-142 are pulled or blocked. So the claim that "no documented fallback the maintainer already thought through" exists is false.

(b) The fix would add a known defect. All seven flagged stamps are `due:none`, because each is a dated first-hand post. L136 explains this: re-reading it next year cannot change it. `source-freshness-format.md` L110 says: "a `due:none` stamp whose `fallback:` says 'escalate if X changes' is a defect on sight. Nothing re-opens a `due:none`." The judge's harm is "if later pulled or disputed", which is exactly that kind of standing order. The job of watching whether Martin's position moves already has an owner: the Stance `would-move-it` line and the OODA roster (question, roster, last-run).

(c) The counting is wrong. The block has 8 source stamps (L136-143), not 7. Seven lack a fallback (L136-142), not 6. The fix says "6 stamp lines at L136-142", which is 7 lines.

(d) This is not a regression. `git diff 324b81d7` shows no changes to any martin-* source line. The Quality row records "technical PASS" at 324b81d7 on these same lines, so the judge is filing a BLOCKING finding against text a previous technical judge passed. `git log -S fallback:` shows the lines have had this shape since they were created (a2f5e9c2).

(e) Scope and severity. §11's scope list names "lecture, exercise, module, reference". This page is a supplementary, the quieter optional tier. No tool enforces a per-stamp fallback: `validate-backing.js` and `source-freshness.sh` never check for it. The gap is in maintainer-block bookkeeping, never reaches a student, and cannot produce a wrong sentence in the body. Calling it BLOCKING overstates the harm. / harm: The finding does not survive. (1) The canonical spec at curriculum/source-freshness-format.md, in its Durable-account variant (L81-100), has a worked example of a `result:OK due:none` first-hand practitioner stamp: Ronacher/MiniJinja at L95. That example carries NO `fallback:` clause. All seven flagged stamps are exactly this shape: `result:OK due:none`, [practitioner direct], dated first-hand posts. The body frames them as a learning journey rather than as current practice. So the format owner approves fallback-less durable-account stamps. The audit script (source-freshness.sh) does not enforce `fallback:` either; only its header comment mentions it. (2) §11(3) asks for a fallback 'if specific source doesn't hold at verification'. Verification has already run: every stamp is result:OK, and due:none means nothing reopens them. A fallback here would be a standing order addressed to a process that never runs, the same shape §2b warns about. (3) Harm lens (d): a fallback already covers the specific risk the judge names ('if any of the other tweets is later pulled'). The martin-security-now line (L143) carries a page-level source-access note that covers 'every quote above' and ends 'fallback: quote from the transcript and the mirrors instead of the X permalinks.' That is the pulled-tweet fallback for all the X stamps, written once rather than seven times. Adding it to each line would be a no-op duplicate. (4) Harm lens (a/b): the harm is a restatement of the rule ('the safety net the rule exists to pre-build is missing'), not a consequence. No student reads the backing block. The page is supplementary, and the maintainer has marked supplementary pages card-exempt, which lowers the stakes. (5) Factual check: the judge's count is wrong. There are 8 stamps (L136-143), and 7 of them lack an inline fallback (L136-142), not '6 of 7'. grep -c 'fallback:' on the file returns 1.
